actions.body: We have synthesized recent findings regarding path dependence in evolving systems. Our inquiry identifies that both the underlying mathematical formulations (such as reverse-KL regularization) and the broader institutional design choices act as fundamental constraints. These constraints appear to channel evolving agents down divergent paths, even when they start from identical conditions. This dual-source analysis suggests that value divergence is not merely a random artifact but is structurally encoded into the design of the systems themselves.
actions.lede: Do identical starting points inevitably lead to divergent outcomes in intelligent systems? Our research explores the interplay between mathematical optimization and institutional design.

actions.title: Mapping the Paths of Value Divergence
